deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of lecture or study notes on ancient Greek history, in German Kurrent. It continues the previous page's account of Lycurgus' Spartan constitution. The script is not obviously Gauss's mature hand, and the bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816' has nothing to do with the content.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) Because of Lycurgus' institutions the Spartan nation could not advance further in culture. It was no blessing for the rest of Greece that such a state arose.
(2) Such a people had to turn to conquest. After Lycurgus' death the Spartans became entangled in wars with their neighbours, above all the Messenian wars, of which three are counted.
(3) First Messenian War, 743-724 (BC). The Messenian king Aristodemus defended himself bravely. The war turned on the border fortress Ithome, placed in the notes 'on the Taygetus range'. Sparta could not take it easily, but finally won. The Messenians were beaten and their king killed himself. Messenia was made tributary and had to hand over half the yield of its lands to Sparta.
(4) During this war the college of Ephors was founded at Sparta. The ephors acted as deputies of the kings and stood between king and people.
(5) Second Messenian War, 685-668. After Aristodemus' death the Messenians had abolished the kingship. Their leader Aristomenes fought bravely, was twice captured by the enemy and twice escaped. The sentence breaks off ('Sie standen an[?]...') and continues on the next page with the alliance with the Arcadians.

There are no derivations to reconstruct. The only numerical content is the traditional chronology. By my own arithmetic, the war lengths are 743-724 = 19 years and 685-668 = 17 years.
errors: Historical (not mathematical) slip: Mount Ithome is a separate mountain in Messenia, not part of the Taygetus range (Taygetus divides Laconia from Messenia).
There are no mathematical errors because there is no mathematics on the page.

results.what: Traditional dates of the First (743-724 BC) and Second (685-668 BC) Messenian Wars, after Pausanias' chronology
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient tradition (Pausanias); standard in 18th-19th c. textbooks

results.what: Founding of the ephorate during the First Messenian War
results.modern_name: Origin of the Spartan ephorate (tradition attributing it to King Theopompus)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine ancient-history notes, probably copied from a lecture or textbook and possibly not in Gauss's own hand. It contains no mathematical content at all.

checkable.asserts: The First Messenian War as dated on the page lasted 19 years.
The Second Messenian War as dated on the page lasted 17 years.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: '...zu kriegerischen [?] Zwe[?] / von Hellas fortgehen' is probably better read as '...zu keinem höhern Grad / von Kultur fortgehen' (tentative). The image shows 'Gra..' at the line end and 'von Kultur' at the start of line 2.

Line 6-7: likely reads '...mit ihren Nachbarn in Kriege verwickelt, aber durch die Kriege mit Messeniern sind sie berühmt'. 'Messeniern' is written once in the line, with a struck-through variant and an interlinear correction; it is not repeated three times.
'der sich mit großem Muth vertheidigte' is confirmed. 'Ithome' and 'Taygetus' are underlined in the manuscript, as are 'Aristodemus' and 'Aristomenes'.
'Die Spartaner konnten sie [-lange-] leicht nicht einnehmen': the deleted word is above or under 'leicht', which is consistent with the transcription.
'Stellvertreter der Könige, und ihre Geschäfte [?] zwischen dem König und Volk': the missing verb is perhaps 'theilten sie' or similar. This is uncertain.
The final line ends 'Sie standen an[?] in', which continues on the next page as 'Verbündung mit den Arkadiern'. A possible reading of the whole phrase is 'Sie standen in Verbündung...'.
